title: Event Loop Blocking and Catastrophic Regex (ReDoS)
platform_conditions: Node.js runtime single-threaded event loop; also applies to browser main threads sharing the same regex engine behavior
security_mechanism: JavaScript runs request handlers on one event loop thread: a single long-running synchronous call stalls every concurrent request. Regex patterns with nested quantifiers over overlapping alternations (e.g. /^([a-zA-Z0-9]+)*$/) backtrack exponentially on a crafted near-match input, so one 50-byte string can pin the loop for minutes -- and there is no built-in match timeout in V8. The same unbounded-work shape appears in synchronous CPU loops and in Buffer.alloc(attackerLength): the allocation is zero-filled synchronously, while Buffer.allocUnsafe returns uninitialized memory that can leak process-internal bytes into responses.

source_sink_clues.source: User-supplied subject strings matched against fixed patterns, attacker-supplied patterns (search features), declared lengths/sizes in protocol headers driving allocations.
source_sink_clues.sink: RegExp .exec/.test/.match on untrusted input with nested-quantifier patterns; long synchronous loops in request handlers; Buffer.alloc or Buffer.allocUnsafe sized from input

tracking_guards: Check subject length is capped before matching and patterns avoid nested quantifiers over overlapping classes; check a worker thread or a timeout-wrapped execution isolates untrusted matches; check allocations use fixed or validated maximum sizes and Buffer.alloc (not allocUnsafe) for response-visible buffers.
not_candidate_when: The pattern is linear (no nested quantifiers) and inputs are length-bounded, the match runs in a worker pool with a deadline, or the buffer size is a compile-time constant independent of input.
synthetic_safe_example: /* use linear regex or set timeouts */
